tasks.short: Determine currency catalog design and audio direction

steps.what: Enter currency sources and sinks
Determine the catalog and its prices
Draft menu design from the catalog rows

loop.input: catalog rows and the menu template
loop.output: menu lines whose price equals the row
loop.check: Every menu item id is on the catalog and the price matches
loop.stop: Drop a line with no item id, and stop the audio section if mood is empty
loop.why_not_simpler: Menu wording is not a fixed label list, but the price must not change

steps.what: Set the audio direction in words
Review supplementary virtual features with production
Sign the supplementary features version
File the signed virtual features

tasks.design: Price, item id, source and sink are rows on a {SPREADSHEET}. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts the menu design and the audio direction only from those rows plus a mood field the designer wrote. The designer signs the supplementary feature set, and {PROJECT} shows that version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Currency and the catalog lived in sheets that the menu text did not cite, so a price could change and the menu still showed the old one.
tasks.enabler_now: An item id can be shared by the sheet and the note, so a price in the note can be checked against the row.
tasks.still_hard: What the currency should feel like, and the audio direction, is still a design judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The designer sets prices and the mood, and rejects a catalog that is only a list.

ambition.what: Re-sign the catalog when a price row changes, not only at the feature milestone

tasks.altitude: Less retyping between the sheet and the note. Price and audio calls stay. The designer can refuse a menu line whose item id is not on the sheet.

reach.task: Implement the signed catalog and menu
reach.learn: Which item ids and prices are signed and which audio notes are still open

evidence.claim: Currency and item catalogs in a mid-size studio are sheets. Menu wording and audio direction are written judgements on top of those rows.
A note can copy a price from a catalog row. It must not invent a price, and the designer still signs the set.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when the signed feature set is filed. Live economy tuning after release is a later task.

Input contract: item id, price, source, sink, menu label, audio mood, and feature id. Producer of price and mood is the game designer. A menu line with no item id is dropped. If the sheet is empty the designer types the rows and marks them manual.
The spreadsheet and the document template are configured before custom code. No live store is updated from this task.
unknowns: Whether any price is real money rather than a virtual currency.
Who owns audio if it is not the designer.
research_questions: What share of menu labels have no item id?
How often is a signed price later changed?

already_counted.description: Price decisions stay with the designer and are not deducted again
Designer edits menu lines whose wording misses the catalog

incremental.description: Keep item ids aligned when the catalog gains a new source or sink

approvals.approved_version: supplementary feature set signed in this review
the same signed supplementary feature set

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes prices stay as prose, so the note is written by hand. The high case assumes rows exist but every price and the audio direction are still chosen and signed by the designer. Store operations are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and revise initial game sketches

steps.what: Read the brief for the initial sketches
Prepare initial sketches in graphical software
Revise sketches using three-dimensional design software
Show the sketches in a review
Sign which sketches to keep
File the sketches that were signed

tasks.design: A sketch brief in {DOCS} holds sketch id, view and what must be readable. The designer still prepares and revises the sketches in {OTHER}, the graphical design software. The review stays in the room. Only the signed sketch version is filed for the team.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sketches were loose files, so a review could talk about a picture that was not the one later used.
tasks.enabler_now: A sketch id can be the name of the file and the brief, so the review is about one version.
tasks.still_hard: The drawing and the revision of the drawing stay with the designer.
tasks.human_edge: The designer decides the pose, the camera and when a sketch is good enough.
tasks.altitude: Sketching time stays. The change is a signed version instead of a loose file. The designer can refuse to file a picture with no brief.

reach.task: Take the signed sketch into a layout
reach.learn: Which sketch version was kept and which views were rejected

evidence.claim: Initial game sketches are drawn and revised by a person in graphical design software, then shown in a review. The drawing is the task.
A version label can tie a file to a brief. It does not draw or revise the sketch, and this task does not ask a model to do that.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when the signed sketch is filed. Finished art is out of scope.
Input contract: sketch id, brief id, view name, dimension, and status. Producer is the game designer. A file with no brief id is not filed. A verbal brief is typed as a view name and marked manual.

The meeting prior counts people in the room while the designer draws. The statement is graphical design software plus a review. Drawing stays on the screen. The software save and the document store version label are tried before custom code. No step generates the picture.
unknowns: Whether a concept artist draws instead of the designer on some titles.
Which file type the team accepts.
research_questions: What share of sketches have no brief id?
How many revisions does a sketch typically have before sign-off?

already_counted.description: Drawing time on the initial sketches stays inside remaining time
Revision time on the sketches stays with the designer and is not deducted again

incremental.description: Keep brief view names aligned when a new sketch type is added

approvals.approved_version: sketch version signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes briefs are verbal, so names are typed by hand and drawing time does not change. The high case assumes ids exist but every sketch is still drawn, revised and reviewed by a person. Finished art is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Create gameplay test plans for internal and external groups

steps.what: List questions for the gameplay plans
Create gameplay test plans from the fields

loop.input: question rows and the plan template
loop.output: plan sections tied to a build id and a group
loop.check: Each section has a build id, a group type and a pass rule
loop.stop: One pass, then leave a blank where the pass rule is empty
loop.why_not_simpler: Question text varies, but it must stay tied to a field the designer entered

steps.what: Mark internal and external groups
Walk the plans with the test lead
Sign the gameplay plans version
Send the signed plans to the groups

tasks.design: Build id, group type, question and pass rule are fields on a {DOCS} template, with group type limited to internal or external. A bounded draft creates the gameplay test plans from those fields and leaves a blank where a pass rule is missing. The designer signs one plan version, and a {WORKFLOW} task then sends that version to the test groups.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans were copied from the last project, so a question could survive after the build it referred to was gone.
tasks.enabler_now: A build id and a group type can be fields, so a section can be checked against them.
tasks.still_hard: Which question is worth a group time, and what counts as a pass, is still a design judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The designer sets the pass rule and decides the plan is fit to send.

ambition.what: Refresh the gameplay test plan when the build id changes, not only once a year

tasks.altitude: The yearly rewrite becomes a check of fields and a signature. The designer can refuse a plan that has a question with no pass rule.

reach.task: Run the signed gameplay test plan
reach.learn: Which questions are in the signed plan and which groups they are for

evidence.claim: A gameplay test plan in a mid-size studio is a document: build, questions, pass rules, and which group is internal or external. Someone signs it before it goes out.
A template can lay out sections from fields the designer entered. It should leave a blank rather than invent a pass rule, and the plan is not sent unsigned.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when the signed plan is sent to the groups. Running the tests is a different task.

Input contract: plan id, build id, group name, group type as internal or external, question, and pass rule. Producer of questions and pass rules is the game designer. Producer of group name may be the test lead. A section with an empty pass rule is left blank and blocks the signature. If questions arrive as prose, the designer types them and marks the row manual.
The document template and the workflow task are configured before custom code. External groups are not given a login by this task. The plan does not record how a person performed.
unknowns: Whether an external group is a vendor.
Who may add a question besides the designer.
research_questions: What share of old plans cite a build that no longer exists?
How often is a pass rule missing?

already_counted.description: Designer rewrites plan sections whose pass rule was too vague
Walkthrough time with the test lead stays and is not deducted again

incremental.description: Update group types and the plan template when a new test group is added
Test lead corrects a group name the form rejected

approvals.approved_version: gameplay test plan version signed for this build
the same signed gameplay test plan version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes questions stay as prose, so the plan is still written by hand. The high case assumes fields exist but every pass rule is still written and the plan is still signed. Time spent running the tests is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Provide test specifications to quality assurance staff

steps.what: Read the design rules the specifications must cover
Write test specifications from the rule list

loop.input: rule rows and the specification template
loop.output: rows whose rule id is on the signed list
loop.check: Every rule id is on the signed list and the expected result equals the designer field
loop.stop: Drop a row with no rule id or an empty expected result
loop.why_not_simpler: The expected result is a sentence the designer must supply, so a lookup cannot write it

steps.what: Check specifications against the rule list
Walk specifications with quality assurance staff
Staff confirm the specifications are runnable
Sign the specifications version
Provide the signed specifications to staff

tasks.design: Each specification row in {DOCS} has rule id, step, expected result and build id, taken from the signed design. A bounded draft fills the specification from those fields and drops a row with no rule id. The designer signs the set. A {WORKFLOW} task then provides that version to quality assurance staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specifications were pasted from the design document, so a step could describe a rule that had already changed.
tasks.enabler_now: A rule id can be checked, so a specification row cannot cite a rule that is not on the signed list.
tasks.still_hard: What the expected result should be is still a design judgement, not a copy of the rule title.
tasks.human_edge: The designer states the expected result and signs the set the staff will run.

ambition.what: Issue a specification when a design rule changes, instead of a batch at the end of the milestone

tasks.altitude: Less pasting from the design. The expected result and the signature stay. The designer can block a row with no rule id.

reach.learn: Which rule ids are covered and which expected results the designer signed

evidence.claim: Test specifications are written from design rules and handed to quality assurance staff. The expected result is a design call. The handoff is a document.
A template can place a rule id and a step from fields. The expected result still has to be the one the designer entered, and the set is not sent unsigned.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when the signed specifications are provided to quality assurance staff. Executing the tests is their task.

Input contract: spec id, rule id, build id, step, and expected result. Producer of the rule id is the signed design list. Producer of the expected result is the game designer. A row with no rule id is dropped and not signed. If the design has no rule ids, the designer types them and marks the row manual.
The document template and the workflow handoff are configured before custom code. Staff are not scored or monitored by this task.
unknowns: Whether quality assurance staff already have a case list this must match.
Who signs if the designer is the only person who knows the rule.
research_questions: What share of specification rows cite no rule id?
How often do staff reject a specification as unrunnable?

already_counted.description: Designer rewrites expected results the draft only echoed
Walkthrough time with staff stays and is not deducted again

incremental.description: Keep rule ids aligned when the signed design list is renumbered
Quality assurance staff send back a row they cannot run

approvals.approved_version: test specification version signed for this build
the same signed test specification version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes design rules have no ids, so specifications are still written by hand. The high case assumes ids exist but every expected result is still judged and the set is still signed. Time staff spend running tests is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Sketches stay at the screen. Catalog notes, gameplay test plans and test specifications start from fields and go out only after a signature. The week loses less retyping between the sheet and the handoff.
reach: Quality assurance analysts receive signed gameplay test plans and signed test specifications instead of a pasted document.
Software developers receive the signed catalog and menu, with item ids that match the sheet.
skills_to_grow: State a pass rule and an expected result as fields a plan can check.
Keep a menu price equal to the catalog row it cites.
Leave sketching as a signed file, not a generated picture.
role.ambitious_version: A test plan or a specification without a signature is not sent, and a menu line without an item id is not shown.
